_provenance:
v2, sealed 2026-09-26. Supersedes v1 (2026-09-26, same day -- see git history for the superseded numbers, labelled 'superseded (corpus changed)' in the PR): v1 was built and measured while src/pravrudhi/assets/nyaya/{bns,bnss}_sections.json shipped BNS/BNSS statute text. That text was withdrawn (pravrudhi PR #55, Tag/Lead-2 hold 2026-09-26: fetched from indiacode.gov.in, whose Terms of Use/Copyright Policy prohibit automated access/systematic extraction -- shipping it as a package asset is a materially different act from a research fetch, and no indiacode-scraped text ships until a lawyer's review, parked by the operator until after the MVP, resolves that conflict). The shipped corpus today is IPC + Constitution of India only -- no BNS, BNSS, or CrPC text at all. 

v2 relabeling (decision: Lead-2, 2026-09-26 -- 'recalibrate honestly against the corpus that actually ships'): every case whose v1 expected_ids named a BNS/BNSS document was re-examined by hand against the ACTUAL shipped IPC/COI section text, not against BM25 scores, to decide whether a genuine IPC doctrinal equivalent exists. Three questions (medium-on-topic-bns-deceit-marriage, long-on-topic-arrest-procedure-story, long-on-topic-search-warrant-story) have NO genuine equivalent in IPC + COI alone -- deceit-marriage is prosecuted under IPC 375's judicially-interpreted 'consent' doctrine, not any of its plain-text clauses, and arrest/search-warrant PROCEDURE is CrPC/BNSS subject matter that IPC (an offences code) was never shipped to cover. These three are reclassified kind: on_topic_uncovered (a real, in-domain legal question this specific shipped corpus genuinely cannot answer -- distinct from off_topic, which means unrelated to law at all) with expected_ids: [] -- retrieve() must return nothing for them, exactly like off_topic, but they are kept in the set (not deleted) because they test the 'don't cite what isn't there' behaviour the BNS-shipping mistake itself violated. One question (medium-on-topic-bns-murder-definition) DOES have a genuine, textually-precise IPC equivalent -- IPC 300 (Murder) is literally the section that draws the culpable-homicide/murder intention line the question asks about, alongside IPC 299 (defines culpable homicide) and IPC 304 (its punishment) -- expected_ids updated to those three, no longer BNS-only. Two questions already had a real IPC alternative that remains genuinely relevant (long-on-topic-dowry-death-story: IPC 304B; medium-on-topic-culpable-homicide-not-murder: IPC 304) -- their now-nonexistent BNS alternatives (BNS/Section 80, BNS/Section 105) are dropped from expected_ids as dead references, not replaced, since the IPC alternative was already there and already correct. 

Two further, SEPARATE findings, not BNS-only questions at all: long-on-topic-conspiracy-story (IPC 120B, criminal conspiracy -- a clean, textually exact match: the question is IPC 120B's own definition almost verbatim) and medium-on-topic-remedies-fundamental-rights (COI/Article 32, constitutional remedies -- equally exact) both remain genuinely on_topic with their existing IPC/COI expected_ids UNCHANGED, but the corpus-wide term-frequency shift from removing ~800 BNS/BNSS documents (idf denominators changed for every remaining document, not just BNS ones) now marginally drops both below min_relevance_norm's floor (0.247 and 0.260 respectively, against a 0.28 threshold) even though the doctrinal answer hasn't changed and nothing about min_relevance_norm itself was retuned here. These are measured, honest recall misses -- see the PR's own re-measured numbers -- not hidden by loosening either floor or by re-labeling the ground truth to match current behaviour, which would defeat the point of a calibration set built independently of the implementation it measures. 

Held-out split (Lead-2, addressing R1's in-sample-only concern): every case carries a new split: 'tune'|'report' field, a stratified (by kind) 50/50-ish assignment seeded 20260926 (random.Random(20260926).shuffle per kind bucket, tune gets the ceiling half on an odd count) so both splits are representative across on_topic/on_topic_uncovered/off_topic/off_topic_verbose. No rule or threshold was retuned in this pass (min_relevance_norm stays 0.28, unchanged from issue #51's own comparison) -- the split exists so a FUTURE retuning pass has a held-out report half to report against, and so today's re-measurement can be shown on both halves rather than only in aggregate. 

v1's own text, preserved for history: Hand-built and sealed 2026-09-26 for issue #51 (length-aware relevance floor). Every question is invented; every expected_ids entry names a real document in src/pravrudhi/assets/nyaya/*.json (IPC, COI, BNS, BNSS -- BNS/BNSS since withdrawn, see above), checked by hand against that document's own text before this file was committed. Written and committed BEFORE any candidate rule (self-score normalisation / term-coverage / top-1-top-2 margin) was run against it. expected_ids: [] means a genuinely uncovered question -- retrieve() should return nothing, not the nearest noise. kind: on_topic (a real question with a real match), off_topic (short, unrelated, no shared legal vocabulary), off_topic_verbose (unrelated but padded with real corpus vocabulary -- the false-citation risk issue #51 is about).

cases.question: What is the punishment for murder under section 302?
equality before law
right to life and personal liberty
several persons common intention liability
If several people act together in furtherance of a shared common intention to commit a crime, is each one of them liable for the whole act as if he alone had done it?
A man promises marriage to a woman purely to get her to agree to sexual intercourse, never intending to actually marry her. What offence does that fall under in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita?
Under the new criminal code, when does an act that causes death cross the line from culpable homicide into murder, in terms of the intention behind it?
Which fundamental right protects a citizen's freedom of speech and expression, and their right to assemble peaceably without arms?

A young married woman dies from burns within a year of her wedding, and her family says that in the weeks before her death her in-laws had been harassing her for more dowry money, refusing to let her visit her parents and constantly demeaning her in front of relatives. Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, what offence captures a death like this where cruelty over dowry preceded it?

When a police officer goes to arrest a suspect who is standing quietly and does not resist or try to run, is the officer still required to physically touch or confine the person, or can an arrest happen just by announcing it, and does it matter if the person being arrested is a woman?

Suppose a Magistrate has reason to believe that someone is being kept confined against their will in circumstances that amount to a criminal offence, in some house on the edge of town, and the family wants to know whether the Magistrate can issue a warrant for a search of the place and have that person recovered, and who exactly is allowed to carry out that search once the warrant is issued.
How do I file a patent application in Germany?
What's the process for registering a trademark in the United States?
What's a good recipe for chicken biryani?
What is the applicable statute for bns69?
What is the applicable statute for bns69, considering the Governor and the President?
What is the applicable statute for bns69, considering the Governor, the President, the Council of Ministers, and the State legislature?

I run a small business and I'm trying to understand the European Union's data privacy rules for handling customer records -- specifically, do citizens there have a personal right to liberty and equal protection of the law the way people talk about fundamental rights, and does the State have any duty to protect that?

In the United Kingdom's system of government, is there anything like a Council of Ministers that advises the monarch the way a Governor is advised in a state, and does the head of state there have discretion the way a President or a Governor might, or is it always bound by ministerial advice?

My trademark application was rejected and I want to appeal it -- separately, if a person is arrested by a Magistrate and taken into custody, and later a warrant is issued for a search of their house, does any of that affect a pending civil registration matter like mine?

Two colleagues secretly agree between themselves to commit a serious offence that carries a sentence of life imprisonment, and they never actually go through with any further act beyond the agreement itself -- assuming there's no separate provision punishing that particular conspiracy, is the agreement by itself enough to be punished, and how severely?

If someone causes a death intending only to cause an injury likely to cause death, but the case does not meet the stricter definition of murder, what is the punishment for that lesser form of culpable homicide?
If the State violates one of a citizen's fundamental rights, which article lets that citizen go directly to the Supreme Court for a writ like habeas corpus or mandamus?
Can you help me book a flight to Tokyo next month?
